scope: Compiler-generated boxed nominal root copy callbacks qualified through local scheduler packets and cached results; source-level recursive workers remain rejected

implementation.compiler: RecursiveRecordOps::copyReference uses construction/read physical layout and nominal token; checked ABI supplies the receiving invocation and stops on faults/cancellation
implementation.runtime: Versioned private recursive_transfer bridge acquires a lease from an exclusively accessed live source invocation and imports its complete immutable graph transactionally
implementation.publication: A nonnull transferred root is required before storing output; stopped/failed/expected-error destinations preserve output and existing error state
implementation.ownership: Packet input, cached result and independent observer copies retain all nested backing without changing immutable pointer values; duplicate imports reuse destination owners
implementation.separation: No recursive source admission, continuation frame or task entry generation changes; tests use trusted C++ scheduler descriptors and ABI adapters around generated callbacks

coverage: Generated construction/copy/read paths for numeric recursive lists, scalar captured functions, duplicate-environment function arrays and array-mediated trees
Input backing remains readable after producer settlement
Cached results support repeated and independent observation without duplicate destination owners
Observed roots survive group/core destruction and onward submission into a new scheduler
Modeled allocation failure sweeps preserve output; packet construction, cached publication and observation failures clean up managed owners
Cancellation, deadlines, scheduler admission failure and worker body faults do not expose successful results
Wrong nominal roots, unknown pointers, missing/faulted/settled source contexts rejected
Cancelled/faulted/settled/expected-error receiving contexts preserve output and prior error state
Emitter rejects malformed operand types and out-of-range nominal identities
Existing handoff depth/resource/concurrency checks, generated ownership bridges, source/callable/function-array execution and recursive frontend rejection regressions
qualification.test_development: Initial scheduler assertions read task failure before the group primary failure; corrected to follow existing scheduler tests. Expected-error destination coverage also motivated an explicit nonnull-result publication branch in the generated copy callback. Final qualification includes both corrections.
qualification.format: Changed C++ ranges formatted; RecursiveRecordEmitterTests.cpp and RecursivePacketBridgeTests.cpp pass clang-format --dry-run --Werror; git diff --check passes

limitations: Boxed-root copy primitive only: source-level recursive spawn/await, continuation frames, inline-root boxing and compiler-generated task descriptors still need integration
Scheduler backing/environment budget accounting is not integrated for these recursive graphs yet; no complete scheduler admission claim
Stored functions are retained and inspected, not invoked by the new scheduler component tests
Private source/raw-root transfer requires exclusive live source access; a retained lease is required to import after producer settlement
Nominal keys, descriptors and code entries are trusted compiler/runtime metadata, not a public dynamic callback or C/C++ ABI
Expected-error payload transport, GPU placement, distributed execution and external-language integration remain separate work
Existing graph, call-depth, stack and allocation limits remain in force
No full-suite, performance or non-macOS-ARM64 qualification claim
